stages.name: Beyond reach
stages.desc: No Somali pirate attacks off its coast

stages.name: Attacks offshore
stages.desc: Somali pirates strike ships in or near its waters

stages.name: Pirate coast
stages.desc: Pirate gangs launch raids and hold hijacked ships here

stages.name: Fighting back
stages.desc: Hosts navies, patrol aircraft, pirate trials or prisons

stages.name: Threat receded
stages.desc: Attacks have stopped; patrols and vigilance remain

states.name: India
timeline: Ships bound for India's west coast cross the Arabian Sea unmolested
India's navy deploys to the Gulf of Aden in October
Indian warships capture over a hundred pirates near the Lakshadweep islands
Pirates no longer reach the Indian coast
INS Kolkata retakes the Ruen in March and brings thirty-five pirates to Mumbai

states.name: Somalia
timeline: Siad Barre's regime falls in January; the state collapses and its coast goes unpoliced
Armed groups calling themselves coastguards seize foreign fishing boats for 'fines'
Afweyne's Hobyo–Harardhere network starts hijacking merchant ships for ransom
The Islamic Courts briefly suppress piracy, until Ethiopia drives them out in December
Eyl, Hobyo and Harardhere hold dozens of hijacked ships at anchor
Somali pirates hold 1,016 hostages in a single year, the all-time peak
A federal government is formed; EU NAVFOR strikes pirate stores on the beach
Only fifteen attacks all year; Afweyne announces his 'retirement' in Hobyo
The tanker Aris 13 is seized off Alula, the first merchant hijacking since 2012
Attacks fade again; no merchant ship is taken for six years
Pirates seize the bulk carrier Ruen in December, as navies turn to the Red Sea
The Abdullah is hijacked in March and freed for a reported five million dollars

states.name: Kenya
timeline: Refugees from Somalia's war cross into Kenya
Pirates attack ships off Kenya and southern Somalia
Kenya convicts ten Somali pirates, the region's first piracy trial
The Saudi supertanker Sirius Star is seized 450 miles off Mombasa
Somali gangs kidnap tourists near Lamu; Kenya's army enters Somalia in October
Attacks off Kenya stop; Mombasa's courts finish their piracy cases

states.name: Tanzania
timeline: Coastal shipping to Dar es Salaam is untroubled
Pirates range south into Tanzanian waters
The pirates no longer reach this far south

states.name: Somaliland
timeline: Somaliland declares independence in May; unrecognised, but largely at peace
Somaliland's courts jail pirates; a UN-supported prison opens at Hargeisa
Few new pirates to try; Somaliland's coastguard keeps watch at Berbera

states.name: Oman
timeline: Ships sail the Arabian Sea along Oman's coast unmolested
Pirate motherships carry skiffs into the Arabian Sea off Oman
Attacks off Oman peak; Salalah becomes a port of call for the navies
The Arabian Sea is quiet again

states.name: Djibouti
timeline: A small port state at the mouth of the Red Sea, with a French garrison
Warships hunting pirates refuel and resupply at Djibouti
The Djibouti Code of Conduct on piracy is signed in January
Japan opens its first overseas military base since 1945, to fight piracy
Djibouti honours Kiyoshi Kimura for his fishing project, Japanese press report

states.name: Eritrea
timeline: Eritrean rebels take Asmara; independence from Ethiopia follows in 1993
Pirates push into the southern Red Sea near the Bab el-Mandeb
The southern Red Sea falls quiet again

states.name: Iran
timeline: Iranian dhows trade along the coast of Arabia and Africa
Iran sends warships to escort its ships through the Gulf of Aden
Pirates stop seizing Iranian dhows as motherships

states.name: Pakistan
timeline: Karachi's shipping lanes are far from Somalia's troubles
Pakistan's navy joins the multinational counter-piracy force CTF-151
Counter-piracy patrols continue as attacks fade

states.name: Mozambique
timeline: Civil war still rages ashore; it ends in 1992
Pirates hijack the fishing vessel Vega 5 in the Mozambique Channel
The Mozambique Channel is quiet again

states.name: Yemen
timeline: Newly unified Yemen looks over the Gulf of Aden shipping lane
The Gulf of Aden becomes the pirates' main hunting ground: ninety-two attacks
A Yemeni court sentences six Somali pirates to death
Convoys, patrols and armed guards empty the Gulf of Aden of pirates
Houthi forces attack shipping in the Red Sea: not piracy, but it pulls the navies away

states.name: Madagascar
timeline: Far beyond the reach of Somali skiffs
Motherships carry pirates to the waters north of Madagascar
The pirates' southern range collapses

states.name: Seychelles
timeline: Island nation of fishermen and tourism, a thousand miles from Somalia
Pirates seize Seychellois boats and the British yacht Lynn Rival
The Seychelles begins trying pirates; drones and patrol aircraft fly from Mahé
Attacks have ended; a regional anti-piracy centre stays open

states.name: Comoros
timeline: Far beyond the reach of Somali skiffs
Pirates reach the northern Mozambique Channel
The pirates no longer reach the Comoros

events.title: Siad Barre falls
events.text: Clan militias drive the dictator from Mogadishu in January; Somalia has no national government for two decades.

events.title: Somaliland breaks away
events.text: The former British Somaliland declares independence at Hargeisa in May; no country recognises it.

events.title: Ilaria Alpi killed
events.text: An Italian television journalist investigating alleged arms and toxic-waste trafficking is shot dead in Mogadishu.

events.title: The UN leaves
events.text: The last UN peacekeepers withdraw from Mogadishu, leaving Somalia to its warlords.

events.title: Puntland founded
events.text: The north-east declares itself the autonomous state of Puntland, with its capital at Garowe.

events.title: A hired coastguard
events.text: Puntland hires a British security firm to chase foreign trawlers; some of the men it trains later turn to piracy.

events.title: Arta peace conference
events.text: Talks in Djibouti create a transitional government that never controls the country.

events.title: Tsunami exposes waste
events.text: The UN Environment Programme reports broken containers of hazardous waste washed up near Hobyo by the 2004 tsunami.

events.title: Semlow seized
events.text: Pirates hijack a ship carrying UN food aid for tsunami victims off Harardhere and hold it for about a hundred days.

events.title: Courts take Harardhere
events.text: The Islamic Courts Union takes the pirate town and briefly stamps out hijackings.

events.title: First Kenyan trial
events.text: A Mombasa court jails ten Somali pirates captured by a US warship: the region's first piracy convictions.

events.title: Courts ousted
events.text: Ethiopian troops drive the Islamic Courts from Mogadishu in late December; piracy soon returns.

events.title: Food-aid escorts
events.text: French warships begin escorting World Food Programme ships to Somalia's ports.

events.title: Le Ponant seized
events.text: Pirates take a French luxury yacht; after the ransom, French commandos capture six of them ashore.

events.title: Eyl's anchorage
events.text: The fishing village of Eyl becomes a byword for piracy, with hijacked ships anchored offshore.

events.title: Faina hijacked
events.text: A Ukrainian ship carrying thirty-three tanks is seized and held off Hobyo for more than four months.

events.title: Sirius Star seized
events.text: Pirates take a Saudi supertanker with two million barrels of oil, 450 miles off Kenya.

events.title: INS Tabar strikes
events.text: An Indian frigate sinks a suspected mothership; it was a hijacked Thai trawler, and most of its crew died.

events.title: Atalanta launched
events.text: The European Union launches its first naval operation, EU NAVFOR Atalanta, on 8 December.

events.title: Djibouti Code
events.text: Regional states sign the Djibouti Code of Conduct to share information and prosecute pirates.

events.title: Maersk Alabama
events.text: Four pirates seize a US container ship 240 miles off Eyl; Navy snipers free Captain Richard Phillips five days later.

events.title: China's navy arrives
events.text: China's first escort flotilla begins convoys through the Gulf of Aden in January.

events.title: Lynn Rival kidnapped
events.text: A retired British couple sailing from the Seychelles are taken and held for 388 days.

events.title: Harardhere falls
events.text: Islamist fighters take Harardhere; its pirates move their ships up the coast to Hobyo.

events.title: Vega 5 hijacked
events.text: Pirates seize a Mozambican fishing boat deep in the Mozambique Channel and turn it into a mothership.

events.title: India's navy strikes
events.text: Indian warships sink the mothership Vega 5 and capture dozens of pirates in the Arabian Sea.

events.title: Japan's Djibouti base
events.text: Japan opens a base for its anti-piracy patrol aircraft and sailors, its first abroad since 1945.

events.title: Lamu kidnappings
events.text: Somali gangs seize tourists on Kenya's coast; in October, Kenya's army crosses into Somalia.

events.title: Handulle raid
events.text: EU NAVFOR helicopters strike pirate boats and fuel on a Somali beach, its first action ashore.

events.title: A federal government
events.text: Somalia's first permanent government since 1991 is formed in Mogadishu in August.

events.title: Iceberg 1 freed
events.text: Puntland's maritime police free a ship and its crew after nearly three years in captivity.

events.title: The Tuna King
events.text: By his own account, Tokyo sushi-chain owner Kiyoshi Kimura offers boats, training and a buyer for tuna to former pirates.

events.title: Afweyne retires
events.text: The pirate boss Afweyne announces his 'retirement' in Hobyo; Belgian police lure him to Brussels that October.

events.title: Somalia joins IOTC
events.text: Somalia becomes a member of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission, a step toward licensing its own fisheries.

events.title: Naham 3 freed
events.text: Twenty-six fishermen are released after four and a half years as hostages, the longest Somali captivity.

events.title: Ocean Shield ends
events.text: NATO ends its counter-piracy operation in December; the EU's Atalanta carries on.

events.title: Aris 13 seized
events.text: Pirates take a small tanker off Alula, the first merchant hijacking in five years; it is released within days.

events.title: UN mandate lapses
events.text: The Security Council's authority for foreign navies in Somali waters lapses in March, at Somalia's request.

events.title: High Risk Area lifted
events.text: On 1 January the shipping industry withdraws the Indian Ocean High Risk Area for piracy.

events.title: Red Sea crisis
events.text: Houthi forces seize the Galaxy Leader and fire on shipping; warships converge on the Red Sea.

events.title: Ruen hijacked
events.text: Pirates seize a Maltese bulk carrier about 700 miles east of Bosaso, the first merchant hijacking since 2017.

events.title: Abdullah hijacked
events.text: A Bangladeshi bulk carrier is seized 600 miles east of Mogadishu; it is freed in April after a reported ransom.

events.title: Ruen retaken
events.text: Indian commandos retake the Ruen in March, free seventeen crew and capture thirty-five pirates.

chartNote: Share of the area of fifteen present-day coastal states, by their main relationship to Somali piracy each year. Many were attacked and fought back at once; the map shows the role that dominated. Large states (India, Iran, Pakistan) swing the shares. Somaliland is drawn apart from Somalia. Attack figures: ICC International Maritime Bureau.
